report:
**Conclusion**
The claim is false. Mainstream scientific and medical consensus confirms that having an abortion does not increase a woman's risk of developing breast cancer.

**Summary of Evidence**
* **National Cancer Institute (NCI) Consensus:** In 2003, the NCI convened over 100 leading experts to evaluate population, clinical, and animal data. The workshop concluded that induced abortion is not associated with an increased risk of breast cancer (https://www.cancer.gov/types/breast/abortion-miscarriage-risk).
* **Global Meta-Analysis:** A landmark 2004 study published in *The Lancet* analyzed 53 epidemiological studies involving 83,000 women across 16 countries. Researchers concluded that abortion does not raise breast cancer risk, noting that older retrospective studies claiming a link were skewed by recall bias (https://www.nytimes.com/2004/03/25/health/abortions-do-not-raise-risk-of-breast-cancer-study-says.html).
* **National Academies Confirmation:** A 2018 report by the U.S. National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine reaffirmed that abortion has no impact on breast cancer risk, highlighting that higher-quality prospective studies consistently find no link (https://www.cancer.org/cancer/risk-prevention/medical-treatments/abortion-and-breast-cancer-risk.html).
* **Scientific Consensus:** Expert health organizations repeatedly review the evidence and maintain a strong consensus that no scientific evidence supports an abortion–breast cancer link (https://www.cbsnews.com/news/study-no-abortion-breast-cancer-link/).

**Sources**
1. National Cancer Institute: https://www.cancer.gov/types/breast/abortion-miscarriage-risk
2. The New York Times: https://www.nytimes.com/2004/03/25/health/abortions-do-not-raise-risk-of-breast-cancer-study-says.html
3. American Cancer Society: https://www.cancer.org/cancer/risk-prevention/medical-treatments/abortion-and-breast-cancer-risk.html
4. CBS News: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/study-no-abortion-breast-cancer-link/
